technical-summary: Added evaluate_resilient() to CDP client that retries on destroyed execution context during ChatGPT navigation; prompt injector switched to evaluate_resilient and added editor wait via wait_for_function before inject. Reduced login_timeout from 120s to 20s since gpt-auto attaches to already-signed-in browser — the old value consumed the entire open budget and caused opaque TimeoutError.
user-summary-candidate: GPT Auto session opens no longer fail with opaque timeout when a spurious login page is detected, and evaluate calls tolerate mid-flight navigation destroying the JS context

technical-summary: SessionRuntime._call() now uses asyncio.wait_for inside the loop instead of Future.result(timeout) to properly cancel timed-out coroutines. The old behavior left orphan coroutines running after timeout — a session open that declared TimeoutError at 120s could finish 11s later and register an unwanted live session, leaking bindings and CDP processes. Reverted _OPEN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS back to 120.0 now that cancellation is correct.
user-summary-candidate: Session open timeout no longer leaks orphan sessions: timed-out coroutines are properly cancelled instead of being abandoned mid-flight

technical-summary: Moved keep_page_active() call before wait_for_chatgpt_ready() in GptAutoSessionTransport.open_session(). Position matters: it must come after _resolve_workspace (CDP has no page until tab activated) and before wait_for_chatgpt_ready (Chrome throttles occluded renderers, that call polls the page). Without this ordering, a session open can silently fail to keep the page active, then stall during readiness checks if the browser is occluded. Also upgraded failure from debug to warning log level.
user-summary-candidate: GPT Auto session opens now activate renderer before readiness check, preventing silent stalls when the browser window is occluded

technical-summary: Added phase-timestamped diagnostics across gateway session runtime calls, provider transport preparation, GPT Auto session open, CDP commands/waits, prompt injection, and response polling. Disabled GPT Auto login waiting; login is now a precondition and detected login pages fail immediately. Preserved compatibility parameters while removing login-timeout consumption.
user-summary-candidate: GPT Auto no longer waits for login and now emits micro-level elapsed-time logs that distinguish the gateway 120s open watchdog from provider readiness, CDP navigation waits, editor waits, injection, and response polling.

technical-summary: Made GPT Auto editor handoff retry-safe: wait for the ProseMirror editor, clear it, and retry the wait/clear sequence up to five times with bounded backoff when navigation causes the editor to disappear between checks.
user-summary-candidate: GPT Auto now retries the short editor/navigation race during prompt injection instead of failing immediately after a successful readiness check.

technical-summary: Removed generic acp-session and provider-name surface fallbacks from gateway session binding and dispatch. Execution profiles must declare a session surface; GPT Auto now explicitly uses gpt-auto-cdp. Bindings and legacy v1 migration fail closed when no resolved surface exists.
user-summary-candidate: Removed the invalid ACP fallback path so provider sessions persist only their explicitly resolved surface; GPT Auto now binds as gpt-auto-cdp and missing surface identity fails closed.

technical-summary: prepare_provider_session_transport() reused the local variable `surface` to hold prepare_provider_mcp_surface()'s McpLaunchSurfaceResult whenever mcp_entries is not None, clobbering the earlier ResolvedSessionSurface snapshot before PreparedSessionTransport(surface=surface, ...) consumed it. Every gateway session open that passes mcp_entries (the gateway session path always does) hit AttributeError: 'McpLaunchSurfaceResult' object has no attribute 'ref' inside sessions.py._open_session. Fixed by renaming the local to mcp_launch_surface. Also re-applied two pieces of prior work not present in the shared working tree (pi/acp.py's _seed_isolated_models_registry fix for session-based pi ACP launches never seeding PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR with models.json, and pi.yaml's AS27 windows-amd64 harness_observability evidence plus its backing real-binary test) so pi-rig gateway sessions work end-to-end on Windows.
user-summary-candidate: Fixed a bug that made every gateway agent session using MCP tools fail to open with a confusing internal error.

technical-summary: AS49 session resume and AS08 continuation-drift detection were both dormant: (1) SessionOpenResult.ag_session_id (the real provider-native session id, e.g. pi's ACP session/new sessionId) was never surfaced in provider-metadata for ACP-backed providers -- AcpAgentSessionTransport.open() now includes it as {'provider-session-id': ...}, matching gpt-auto's existing chat-id/project-id pattern. (2) provider_session_ref was derived via str(open_result), stringifying the whole SessionOpenResult dataclass repr instead of extracting ag_session_id -- fixed in both _open_session and _resume_session, so the stored ref is now a real, usable provider session id rather than a broken repr string. (3) open_session never accepted identity/execution context fingerprints, so every session's binding was permanently stamped with the 'unknown' sentinel -- both AS49's resume identity-match (CON-AGW-114/115) and AS08's continuation-drift check (CON-AGW-101) were structurally unreachable. Added identity_context_fingerprint/execution_context_fingerprint threading through open_session -> build_session_record -> build_binding, stamped from the request's own SH02 manifest context_fingerprint at open time (dispatch.py), and forwarded context_fingerprint from queue/dispatch.py into the session-dispatch path so AS08's continuation check is now live. resume_execution_session now computes a fresh context_fingerprint from the source session's current profile/provider/model resolution (mirroring build_manifest) instead of requiring a caller-supplied value nothing ever produced correctly. (4) Also fixed _resume_session using the caller's raw (usually None) model_id for transport prep instead of defaulting from the source session first, which raised VAL-MODEL-002 on every resume attempt. Verified end-to-end via direct reproduction: harness-native session id now appears in provider-metadata; resume now correctly reaches pi's real session/load RPC with the correct session id (previously never got that far). Standard multi-turn continuation regression-checked clean with the new AS08 check active. Resume itself is still blocked by a separate, unrelated issue: the installed pi binary (0.83.0) rejects session/load with 'Invalid params', vs the evidence-pinned 0.82.1 -- a pi-side protocol/version drift, not part of this fix.
user-summary-candidate: Fixed several session-resume plumbing bugs: the real provider session id (e.g. pi's session id) is now visible in session metadata, and the resume-safety checks that were silently disabled now actually work.

technical-summary: AS49 session resume was structurally impossible end-to-end even after the earlier fingerprint/ref fixes in this same session: SessionRuntime._cleanup_handle_runtime unconditionally shutil.rmtree'd a session's entire isolated per-request runtime root on close, which is where pi (and potentially other ACP providers) writes its own native, durable session history (PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR/agent/sessions/*.jsonl) -- verified directly by inspecting a live, still-open session's runtime dir before any cleanup ran. This meant the session data resume needs to seed from was always already gone by the time anyone tried to resume, independent of any other resume machinery being correct. Root cause is entirely self-inflicted: AUDiaGentic redirects PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR to a temp per-request directory instead of pi's natural default (~/.pi/agent, never touched by us), then deletes that directory -- a standalone `pi` session run by a user is unaffected since it uses the untouched default. Fix: added PreparedSessionTransport.runtime_preserve_relpaths (provider-declared, via a new provider-keyed registry in public_execution.py mirroring the existing observability-hook-factory pattern; pi declares pi/agent/sessions) and a new _cleanup_preserving helper in sessions.py that walks the runtime root deleting everything except declared-durable subpaths, instead of wiping it wholesale. Resume itself was also missing a request_runtime_root entirely (resume_execution_session never established one, unlike ordinary queued dispatch), so PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR was never even set for a resume attempt; fixed by having _resume_session reuse the SAME preserved runtime root from the original opening request (source_record["request-ids"][0]) rather than allocating a fresh one, which is also the more semantically correct choice (same isolated environment continuing, not a new one). Also fixed foundation/transports/acp.py's open_resumed() silently discarding the real provider-side rejection reason (RequestError's own message is always the generic JSON-RPC string; the actual reason lives in .data) -- this swallowing is what made the true root cause take significant investigation to find instead of being immediately visible in the error. Verified end-to-end for real: opened a pi-rig session, stated a fact, closed it, resumed it into a new session, and confirmed the resumed session correctly recalled the fact stated before the close. Standard multi-turn continuation regression-checked clean.
user-summary-candidate: Fixed session resume for real: closing a session no longer deletes the data needed to resume it later, and a resumed conversation now genuinely remembers what was said before it was closed.

technical-summary: Migrated persisted gateway execution-session records to grouped v3 provider, timing, policy, and activity fields with v1/v2 compatibility migration and accessor-based reads; updated schema, error resolution, and gateway tests.
user-summary-candidate: Gateway execution sessions now use the v3 grouped contract while safely reading and migrating older records.
